situation (example wording): "Can I see murders rolling over 12 months nationally?", "murders rolling over 12 months since 2019", "violent crime rolling over 12 months in Iowa City", "Dallas and Houston murders rolling over 12 months since 2025"
what the app does today: Declined ("a state or national sum of several crimes, a breakdown, a change or a ranking", "Violent crime totals are whole years only."), or one total for the latest 12 months.
proposed behavior: "Rolling over 12 months" (or another number of months) is a series of rolling totals by month, from Current Trends: each month's value is the total of that month and the months before it in the window. A window with a month that has no figure is blank, never a shorter sum. The first row is the January of the year named ("since 2019": January 2019, window February 2018 to January 2019); with no timespan named, the first January with a full window (January 2018, window February 2017 to January 2018). A span that reaches before the data starts at that January and says the months outside the data. The title reads back the question ("January 2018 to August 2026 Rolling 12-Month Murders by Month, United States"); no note says what a rolling total is. Only blank months are noted ("No figure is available for March 2020: every 12-month window containing that month is shown blank, not zero."). One place, a state or the nation, or several agencies side by side. For a state or the nation the sample depends on how far back the windows reach: if the first window starts in January 2025 or later (inside the published sample's life) it is the published Consistent Reporting Agencies (the sample flag), as on crimeindex.org; if it starts before 2025 it is the agencies with a figure in every month the series needs (the first window's first month through the latest month; an agency-month's figure is Current Trends' final panel's, else its monthly panel's), summed month by month. Their number and the people they cover are said once ("This counts only the 547 Consistent Reporting Agencies, covering roughly 110 million people, that reported every month from February 2017 through August 2026."). "The last 12 months" stays one total. Counts only; averages, indexes and rates are separate.
exact default or choices offered: The title, notes only for blank months, then the Source line.
why: Jeff 2026-11-19 (through the coordinator): build rolling totals; start at the beginning of the next first full year; notes silent except blank months.
